title_en: Timber Building Structures in Chosen Korea - A Case Study on Geunjeongjeon and Injeongjeon

journal.title: Journal of Architectural and Planning Research

scope: Comparative study of two monumental palace halls, with Chinese and Japanese comparisons. It is not a measured survey or a source for every Joseon building type.
relevance: Useful structural sections and discussion for reading the relationship between roof tiers, supports, and tall interiors. Primary survey verification is still needed before adopting dimensions or assigning historical states.

notes.statement: Guo describes Geunjeongjeon and Injeongjeon as presenting two exterior stories while having single tall interiors with additional eaves. The Geunjeongjeon section and accompanying discussion distinguish inner and outer column networks, including tall inner supports and upper outer columns carried on tie beams.
notes.scope: The two halls discussed by this article; the visually inspected structural example is Geunjeongjeon. Figure 4's caption includes 1865, but its historical attribution has not been independently verified or adopted as a building-state record.

notes.statement: Guo reports different central, intermediate, and end-bay spans in Geunjeongjeon and proposes that its end bay may have served as a design module. The article calls for further comparison of Korean timber grading, then discusses a historical proposal whose influence on building regulations the author leaves unresolved.
notes.scope: The author's analysis and stated uncertainty in this 2005 article. Neither the proposed module nor a historical-unit conversion has been adopted as a modeling default or measured building observation.
